title: Latency smoothing: kernel exploratory journal
body:
Purpose
Quick, informal journal of the week: exploratory ideas and results for reducing 99th percentile token latency spikes that show up during mixed small/long-session workloads. This is a working capture — messy notes, measurements, and action items for the kernel/KV/batching cross-team sync.

Context / why this felt important this week
- Over the past three weeks we've seen a recurring pattern: overall throughput is fine but 99p tail increases ~20–40ms during bursts with a high fraction of short-chat calls interleaved with a few long-context requests.
- Hypothesis: a combination of micro-batching jitter, KV cache contention, and kernel scheduling oscillation (priority inversion when a long request reacquires KV state) is amplifying tail latency.

Summary of experiments run (09/12–09/17)
1) Queue smoothing (software token-bucket) 
   - Setup: added a lightweight token-bucket layer before batch formation to spread arrivals from a sawtooth traffic replay.
   - Result: 50% reduction in frequency of 99p spikes in the microbench that replays the customer mix. Mean latency slightly up (~3ms) but tail much tighter.
   - Notes: increased burst_delay param reduces throughput marginally; good candidate for a per-tenant policy.

2) KV shadowing prototype (read-mostly fast-path)
   - Setup: shadow read cache that duplicates hot KV gets into a per-kernel local store for 10s windows. Fallback reads go to global KV.
   - Result: 30% fewer kernel stalls attributable to KV fetches on long requests; CPU cost ~6% higher.
   - Notes: eviction strategy needs more thought, currently LRU is noisy under high churn. Possible to combine with TTL hints from router.

3) Microkernel preemption tweak
   - Setup: allow kernel to preempt long-op batches after N tokens if there are >=M ready short requests in queue.
   - Result: reduced observed priority inversion in synthetic trace, but caused measurable oscillation when arrivals oscillate rapidly — saw repeated preempt/resume thrash causing small additional overhead.
   - Notes: need hysteresis and backoff counters to avoid thrash.

Telemetry highlights (local bench + staging - 09/17)
- Baseline 99p token latency: 420ms. With token-bucket smoothing: 380ms. With KV shadowing: 390ms. Combining smoothing + shadowing: 345ms.
- Throughput under synthetic mix: nominal drop 2–4% when smoothing applied (config dependent).
- CPU burn: +4–7% with KV shadowing; memory overhead per-kernel ~80–120MB depending on model KV footprint.

Open design questions
- Per-tenant vs global smoothing: do we want default smoothing on all tenants? risk of increased cost for latency-insensitive workloads. Proposed: opt-in + adaptive policy based on SLA class.
- KV shadow consistency model: do we accept short-lived staleness for the sake of latency? For generation use-case it seems OK, but reranking/streaming tool-calls may be sensitive.
- Scheduler hysteresis: how to tune preemption thresholds to avoid thrash without reintroducing priority inversion? suggestion: sliding-window counters + exponential backoff.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Aisha: append a simple sliding-window hysteresis to preempt logic, run lab replay across three tenant mixes, report by 2029-09-22.
- Daniel: prototype TTL-hinted KV shadow eviction (use router hints), small PR with perf baseline by 2029-09-21.
- Mateo: add per-tenant smoothing flags to the dev config, enable for two high-SLA tenants in staging, evaluate cost/throughput impact by 2029-09-24.
- Priya: synth workload runner — add a variant that toggles arrival jitter every 30s to stress preemption/backoff behavior; provide test harness by 2029-09-20.
- Li: update observability dashboard to include preempt/resume counters and per-kernel KV hit ratio; coordinate with telemetry infra, target 2029-09-23.

Risks / trade-offs captured in this sprint
- Trade-off between tail and mean: smoothing can help tails but nudges mean latency up slightly; need to align with product SLOs for each tenant class.
- Cost vs latency: KV shadowing reduces stalls but increases CPU and memory; may be fine for Dedicated and some Hosted tiers, questionable for very cost-sensitive free-tier workloads.
- Complexity: adding preemption+hysteresis + shadowing increases runtime surface area and bug surface for kernel state management. Keep experiments behind feature flags.

Meeting notes (09/17 10:00am — kernel sync)
- Quick demo of token-bucket smoothing from Aisha. Team liked the simplicity and the deterministic behavior.
- Daniel cautioned about eviction pathological cases when long-running finetune-like sessions heat many keys.
- Decision: land smoothing behind per-tenant flag, default off for free/low-tier; enable in staging for two tenants (see action items).
- Agreement: KV shadowing is promising; continue with TTL-hint approach and a short-lived pilot on staging.

Scratch ideas & future experiments (brain dump)
- Cohort-aware batching: group small chats from the same tenant into tenant-scoped micro-batches to reduce cross-tenant interference.
- Predictive prefetch: use a lightweight historical predictor to warm KV for the next N tokens for active sessions.
- Hardware-aware scheduling: prefer packing short-chattier requests onto GPUs with higher SM availability; route long-context to nodes with larger NVMe-backed KV if available.

Handoff notes for oncall
- Feature flags: smoothing_flag_v1, kv_shadow_ttl_hint, preempt_hysteresis_v1. All are currently off in prod.
- If tail spikes begin after enabling smoothing: rollback smoothing_flag_v1 and increase token-bucket burst_delay.
- If KV memory climbs unexpectedly: disable kv_shadow_ttl_hint and inspect eviction logs (channel: #serving-runtime-kv).

Closing thought
- This week felt productive: a few complementary knobs (smoothing + KV-shadow) seem to stack well. Next week focus on robustness (hysteresis + eviction) and a small staging pilot.

Appendix: raw short logs from synthetic replay (abbreviated)
- 09/16 14:03:22 sample-run: saw 12 tail spikes in 10m; after smoothing: 3 spikes.
- 09/16 16:11:08 kv-shadow: local hit ratio 87% during steady phase, fell to 62% under churn.
- 09/17 09:45:33 preempt: observed 4 preempt thrash events in 5m with naive thresholds.

Notes to self
- Keep these notes as living doc until pilot completes. Move to playbook once we settle on safe defaults and rollback steps.
